Each column holds -1 at the edge's source (teal) and 1 at its target (accent), so it sums to 0; edge 1, from A to B, gives A -1 and B 1." width="100%"} Rows are nodes and columns are edges: entry `[i][j]` is nonzero when the `i`-th node is an endpoint of the `j`-th edge. In the unoriented matrix both endpoints get `1` (or the edge weight); in the oriented matrix the source gets `-1` and the target `+1`, so each column sums to zero. The oriented incidence matrix `B` factors the Laplacian as `L = B Bᵀ` and underlies network flow, circuit and cycle-space computations. Self-loops give all-zero columns, as in NetworkX's `incidence_matrix()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [oriented]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, mark each edge's source with a negative entry. Default is `False`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether entries hold edge weights instead of `1`. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list[int], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids, edge_ids)`: the matrix as a list of rows (one per node), the node IDs labelling rows, and the edge IDs labelling columns, both in increasing order. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path A-B-C, the oriented incidence matrix multiplied by its transpose gives the Laplacian: ::: {#883a25a9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]).add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) b, nodes, edges = path.incidence_matrix(oriented=True) laplacian = [[sum(b[i][k] * b[j][k] for k in range(len(edges))) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)] b, laplacian == path.laplacian_matrix()[0] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([[-1.0, 0.0], [1.0, -1.0], [0.0, 1.0]], True) ``` ::: :::
